orders.challenge_claim: The row files its dod signal under the beloved address vocabulary when the span's only dod-family bytes are the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object, and three further attributions - verse position, marker location, cross-verse constancy - are imprecise against the bytes.
orders.grounds: Re-derived object-first, not digit-first. The span's only dod-skeleton bytes are דֹּדֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Song.1.2, tier: byte) and דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte); both skeletonize to the vav-less spelling, which is the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object (sweep: 4 verses - MT 1:2, MT 1:4, MT 4:10, MT 7:13 [= WEB 7:12]), and I re-checked both address lists: neither MT 1:2 nor MT 1:4 appears in dodi-exact (24 verses) or dod-family (28 verses). So the signal key naming the dodi address vocabulary names an object this span does not carry - the tier-1 dod address-epithet - which is the five-object blend in its field-level form. Verse position confirmed: the span is Song.1.2-Song.1.4, so oshb:Song.1.4 is its THIRD verse, not its second. Marker location confirmed: in מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) the 2ms marker is the final kaf of אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ; the imperative's own suffix is 1cs, so 'imperative-plus-suffix address' mislocates it (the imperative STEM is 2ms at the pointed-byte tier, which is why this is a wording defect rather than a false attribution). Cross-verse constancy confirmed: MT 1:3 carries the span's densest 2ms evidence - שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ, שְׁמֶ֑ךָ, אֲהֵבֽוּךָ (all tier: byte at oshb:Song.1.3) - and the row splices none of it, while בָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) is 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, left undisclosed and genuinely unsettleable with no morphology layer staged. ONE CORRECTION to the challenge's own framing: the row's boundary argument does not lean on the dod key - its stated tier-1 evidence is the 2ms suffix forms - so the blend is a field-contract defect, not a failed voice attribution.
orders.remedy: Re-key observed_substrate_signals off the dodi address vocabulary to the gendered-form signal class the row actually argues; in boundary_rationale NAME the swept object before any dod word (the defective 'your loves' spelling, sweep: 4 verses); correct 'second verse' to 'third verse'; re-word the MT 1:4 marker as the 2ms suffix on אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (spliced, tier: byte) rather than on the imperative's suffix; splice at least one 2ms form from oshb:Song.1.3 (tier: byte) into the three-verse continuity claim; disclose בָּ֔ךְ as form-2fs / pausal-2ms and unsettleable. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): any dod reference in this row must survive a name-the-object check against the dodi-exact (24 verses) and dod-family (28 verses) lists, neither of which contains MT 1:2 or MT 1:4.

orders.challenge_claim: The row's closing-seam driver is byte-false in position and is voice-identity rather than voice-shift evidence, and no Hebrew at all is quoted from MT 1:6.
orders.grounds: All three arms re-derived and confirmed. MT 1:7 opens הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte; that opener is 1 verse book-wide), and שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) stands as the verse's third and fourth tokens - so 'the she-ahavah-nafshi formula opening Song.1.7' is byte-false in position. Substantively: that formula is tier-1 under the moderate policy but it is HER formula at all five of its verses (sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4) and MT 1:5-1:6 is her voice as well, so across MT 1:6|1:7 it marks voice IDENTITY, not a voice shift; it cannot be the closing driver the row makes it. The seam is real and byte-markable as an ADDRESSEE shift the row never quotes: plural אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, tier: byte) addressing the daughters, against 2ms חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) addressing the man. With no Hebrew spliced from MT 1:6, the row's 'no further addressee change through the end of Song.1.6' rests on the English rendering alone. Tier-4 audit: no modern voice-apparatus heading precedes WEB 1:7, so this seam is not apparatus-derived - the row is clean on that axis. PEER-SIDE FINDING carried forward: the converging primary SUPPORTED this row on precisely the arm that fails, reproducing the byte-false 'formula opening Song.1.7' position - the support item is itself defective.
orders.remedy: Replace the closing driver: argue MT 1:6|1:7 from the addressee flip, splicing אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, tier: byte) against חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte), each tier-labeled; demote the she-ahavah-nafshi formula to what it is here - a same-voice tier-1 anchor confirming her voice continues - and correct the position claim (the opener is הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י). CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the replacement driver must show a marked change ACROSS the seam; a formula attested only in her voice cannot mark a shift out of her voice.

orders.challenge_claim: The single-verse holding is byte-sound, but the formula's byte position is misstated and the 2ms gender claim is asserted on a morphologically ambiguous form whose in-verse disambiguator is never quoted.
orders.grounds: Both arms are byte-confirmed, but the severity is understated - the corrected finding is medium, not low. תִרְעֶ֔ה (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) is a prefix-conjugation form whose 2ms and 3fs readings are graphically identical, and no morphology layer is staged, so the row's 'carries second-masculine-singular marking' is not a byte claim at all. The 2ms reading is in fact secure - fixed by חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) in the same verse, with תַּרְבִּ֣יץ (tier: byte) in parallel - so the CONCLUSION survives while its cited evidence does not. That matters more than 'low': this is the cluster's only single-verse holding, it is filed at HIGH confidence, and its entire rejected alternative rests on a masculine-to-feminine gender flip at MT 1:7|1:8 whose masculine side is asserted on the ambiguous form. Position arm confirmed as in the preceding row (the opener is הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י). Third arm confirmed: 'flips every verb and suffix' is a universal with no adjacent digit and no spliced form, while MT 1:8 in fact carries 6 such markers; the machine universals arm independently flags this sentence. TWO further peer findings: (a) this byte-false formula position appears in TWO rows of this cluster, so it is a CURE CLASS and the correction must be swept, not spot-fixed; (b) the converging primary supported this row asserting the 2ms verb was 'confirmed at byte tier' - a byte confirmation the staged extract cannot yield for this form.
orders.remedy: Splice חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) as the disambiguator that fixes the 2ms reading, and re-cast תִרְעֶ֔ה as form-ambiguous between 2ms and 3fs with no morphology layer staged; correct the formula's position; give the MT 1:8 flip a digit and at least one spliced 2fs form (6 markers at oshb:Song.1.8). Sweep the position correction across every row of this cluster that repeats it. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): every gender claim must rest on a form unambiguous at the pointed-byte tier, or be explicitly held.

orders.challenge_claim: The row argues a four-verse single-addressee unit while leaving the one tier-1 address anchor inside its own span uncited and carrying three of its four verses on the English rendering alone.
orders.grounds: Confirmed. רַעְיָתִֽי (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte) sits INSIDE this row's own span and is the attested tier-1 address anchor of his word for her (sweep: 9 verses - MT 1:9, 1:15, 2:2, 2:10, 2:13, 4:1, 4:7, 5:2, 6:4), re-checked against the inventory; the row neither argues MT 1:9 in prose nor mirrors it into boundary_evidence_refs, and it is the single strongest available warrant for the row's own male-voice reading. The 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte) goes unused with it. Translation-carrying confirmed: no Hebrew is spliced from MT 1:9, MT 1:10 or MT 1:11 - three of the four verses of a four-verse continuity claim. Negation slip confirmed: MT 1:8 opens אִם לֹ֤א (tier: byte), so תֵדְעִי֙ (tier: byte) is neither the unit's opening token nor the bearer of the negation the row's gloss puts inside it. The credit is also correct and I re-audited it: a modern voice-apparatus heading does precede WEB 1:11, and the row declines it on the absence of a gender-marked form - that arm audits clean against apparatus-leaning. PEER-SIDE ADDITION, unraised by either primary: the row's English for MT 1:10 and MT 1:11 stands in straight quotes with a bare numeric ref while carrying verses that have no Hebrew at all, which routes WEB renderings around the curly-quote-plus-inline-web-ref requirement.
orders.remedy: Add oshb:Song.1.9 to boundary_evidence_refs and splice רַעְיָתִֽי (tier: byte) into boundary_rationale as the span's tier-1 address anchor, with the object named and its digit (sweep: 9 verses); splice at least one 2fs form from oshb:Song.1.10 and from oshb:Song.1.11 (tier: byte) so the four-verse continuity stops being translation-carried; re-cut the gloss of תֵדְעִי֙ so the negation sits where the bytes put it, and stop calling it the opening token. In the same pass repair the quote convention: any WEB rendering carried as evidence takes curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the SAME field. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): every verse inside the span must carry at least one spliced tier-labeled form or an explicit hold - MT 1:9, which carries the span's own tier-1 anchor, failed it.

orders.challenge_claim: A voice-shift seam is asserted with no gender-marked form quoted on either side of it, and two of the book's twelve paseq verses sit inside this three-verse span undisclosed.
orders.grounds: Arm 1 upheld; arms 2 and 3 do not survive re-derivation. ARM 1 CONFIRMED: the row asserts a shift out of 2fs address into her first-person voice at MT 1:11|1:12 and splices no Hebrew on either side of it. The 2fs form at the seam is נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte); MT 1:12's only first-person marker is נִרְדִּ֖י (tier: byte), a gender-UNMARKED 1cs possessive standing beside third-person שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ (tier: byte, the melek lexeme - sweep: 5 verses). The row's two spliced quotes sit one and two verses past the seam, so the seam is carried by tier-2 continuity while the moderate policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted at a voice-shift seam - a real medium defect. ARM 2 REFUTED: the paseq layer is a count-only seg inventory, and the unconditional span-relevant disclosure symmetry runs over the PARASHAH set, not over paseq; this row's span-relevant parashah obligation (the SAMEKH at MT 1:14) IS disclosed, and the marks arm returns clean over the whole cluster. A row that makes no paseq claim owes no paseq disclosure, so there is no symmetry gap here. ARM 3 REFUTED on the bytes: the row NAMES its object ('the dodi-exact form') and 24 verses is that object's correct count, with MT 1:13 and MT 1:14 both on the list; the adjacent two-word run is a separate object (byte tier: 2 verses, MT 1:13 and MT 1:14; skeleton tier: 4 verses, adding MT 2:16 and MT 6:3), but the row attaches NO digit to that run, so there is an invitation to slippage and no actual blend to cure. PEER-SIDE FINDING, unraised by either primary: the row's sole stated evidence for its opening verse is an English string attached to a web: ref that is not that verse's WEB rendering at all - a mis-attributed rendering standing where a splice or a verbatim quote belongs.
orders.remedy: Splice נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte) and נִרְדִּ֖י (oshb:Song.1.12, tier: byte) into the seam argument, tier-labeled, and re-cast the seam honestly: the marked 2fs addressee DROPS and no gender-marked first-person form replaces it, so the shift rests on the disappearance of the marked addressee plus tier-2 continuity, with confidence held accordingly. Replace the English at the opening verse with either that verse's verbatim WEB rendering in curly quotes with its inline web: ref, or a spliced tier-labeled Hebrew quote. Leave the paseq segs and the 24-verse digit untouched - both are already correct. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the seam sentence must quote a form from EACH side of MT 1:11|1:12 and must not claim a gender-marked shift the bytes do not carry.

orders.challenge_claim: The exchange's opening is the cluster's best byte evidence, but its closing seam at MT 2:3|2:4 carries no byte evidence, no forward neighbour ref, and is crossed by an unbroken single-speaker configuration the row never discloses.
orders.grounds: Confirmed at byte tier. The opening is sound - הִנָּ֤ךְ (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte, 2fs) against הִנְּךָ֨ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 2ms) is exactly the gender-marked pair the moderate policy asks for. The closing seam is not argued at all: no sentence of the row addresses MT 2:3|2:4, and boundary_evidence_refs carries only a backward neighbour (WEB 1:14), no forward one. The bytes run straight across the cut: 1cs חִמַּ֣דְתִּי and וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי with לְחִכִּֽי (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) continue into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ with 3ms וְדִגְל֥וֹ and עָלַ֖י (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte) - same speaker configuration, no vocative, no address-vocabulary token, no gender-marked addressee change at the cut. A byte-true single-voice run straddling the row's own seam argues continuity AGAINST the row unless disclosed, and it is undisclosed; under the hybrid granularity rule a cut inside a sustained single-voice run needs a tier-1 marker at the cut, and there is none. Secondary arms hold: the row keeps MT 1:17 inside her turn on the English rendering with no Hebrew spliced, and the token it leans on is the qere in the span's one K/Q-bearing verse (4 K/Q notes book-wide, single-witness) that the row simultaneously declares it makes no K/Q claim about; and אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת (oshb:Song.2.1, tier: byte) is gender-unmarked and left unattributed inside a unit whose entire warrant is attributed alternation. CONVERGENCE: this is the SAME core defect as the other primary's item on this row, reached from different evidence - see that ruling.
orders.remedy: (a) BOUNDARY PROPOSAL, explicit boss adoption required - extend the exchange to close at the MT 2:6|2:7 refrain bracket, or re-cut so the single-voice run beginning inside MT 2:3 is not severed. (b) If the cut at MT 2:3|2:4 is retained, disclose the cross-seam single-voice continuity explicitly, add the forward neighbour to boundary_evidence_refs, and lower the confidence. (c) Splice the 1cp forms עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte) and בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte) in place of the English for the MT 1:17 arm, and note the qere status of the other 1cp token in that verse. (d) Attribute MT 2:1 at the tier the bytes support, or record it as held. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the far boundary must name a tier-1 marker AT the cut, or the row must disclose that none exists and hold its confidence accordingly.

orders.challenge_claim: The far boundary at Song.2.3|Song.2.4 is argued from mirrored ken/ken parallelism rather than any tier-1 voice-shift marker, and the strongest rejected alternative never engages the live rival of extending through Song.2.4-Song.2.6 to the Song.2.7 adjuration close.
orders.grounds: SAME DEFECT as the converging item on this row, not a distinct one: both name the unwarranted far boundary at MT 2:3|2:4, and I have upheld it on byte grounds there. This item's DISTINCT and correct contribution is the rejected-alternative gap: the row's only rival is atomizing into single-verse turns, while the live rival - extending through MT 2:4-2:6 to the adjuration bracket that closes the movement - is never engaged, and it is the rival the hybrid granularity rule makes live at this seam. TWO FRAMING CORRECTIONS. First, this item rests its evidentiary weight on the parashah SAMEKH at MT 2:7, called an 'undisclosed cross-seam corroboration signal': that mark is TIER-3 weak, single-witness, never a boundary driver in either direction, and it does not straddle the MT 2:3|2:4 seam - it sits three verses past it and is not in this row's span-relevant disclosure set, which is the SAMEKH at MT 1:14 and IS disclosed (the marks arm returns clean for this row). Using a tier-3 mark as directional evidence toward a later closure is the same tier error the challenge elsewhere polices. The genuine cross-seam device was available at byte tier: the 1cs configuration of oshb:Song.2.3 running into oshb:Song.2.4. Second, the bar on parallelism standing alone as a boundary driver is a distinct rule from the operative-category law this item cites for it. Net: defect real and upheld, grounds substituted, severity unchanged.
orders.remedy: Covered by the work order on the converging item, plus specifically: strongest_rejected_alternative must engage the extension-to-the-refrain-bracket rival and say from BYTES why it is rejected, or the boundary proposal is adopted instead - one sentence, plus the optional second sentence only for the mandated rival disclosure. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the rejected alternative must name the rival the granularity rule makes live at this seam, not only the rival the row can easily refute.

orders.challenge_claim: The Song.2.4 opening is argued from the absence of a formula anchor past Song.2.3 rather than from a positive tier-1 marker, so the row theme-splits a maximal she-voice run that properly spans Song.2.3-Song.2.7; the row's signal entry names a dodi anchor that stands in no verse of its own span; and the Song.2.6 WEB citation is straight-quoted and lower-cases the source's verse-initial word.
orders.grounds: Diagnosis upheld, corrected span refuted. Upheld on bytes: nothing at the 2:3|2:4 junction is a tier-1 in-verse marker -- the last clause of oshb:Song.2.3 and the opening verb of oshb:Song.2.4 hold the same first-person speaker and the same third-masculine-singular referent, with no vocative, no suffix flip and no address-vocabulary anchor AT the cut, so the row's stated driver is anchor-absence plus a topic change (tier-2 continuity reasoning at best, not the tier-1 ground the hybrid granularity rule demands at a cut). Upheld on bytes: the row quotes the Song.2.6 clause with straight delimiters and lower-cases the verse-initial word -- that witness reads “His right hand embraces me.” (web:Song.2.6), and the row's string fails an exact-case substring check while passing case-insensitively; zero curly-quoted WEB runs stand anywhere in this cluster's rows. REFUTED, with the refuting bytes: the corrected span the challenge proposes (Song.2.3-Song.2.7) cannot stand. Song.2.3 is the answering member of an attested tier-1 alternation pair -- רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, tier: byte), his address word for her, answered by דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte), her word for him -- inside the hinnakh/hinnekha exchange that the owner ruling holds whole as one dialogue unit; moving Song.2.3 into a she-voice run would both break that whole-held zone and split an attested anchor pair. The seam is therefore real and inherited from the preceding zone's close; only the row's STATEMENT of it is defective. Signal-entry sub-claim REFINED, not upheld: no dod-family token stands in Song.2.4-Song.2.6 (verified verse by verse), so the challenge's byte observation is right, but the signal field contract records the signal CLASS consulted, and consulting the address-vocabulary class to establish that no anchor survives is within the contract -- the defect is the rationale's reliance on that absence, not the field entry. NEW FINDING (neither primary): the ahavah citation blends units -- the row calls the Song.2.4 form a token and then says 'one of ten', while the true objects are 10 VERSES and 11 TOKENS (MT 8:7 carries two); the parenthetical names verses, the prose object does not.
orders.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the anchor-absence driver with the positive warrant that the preceding unit is a whole-held dialogue exchange closing at Song.2.3, citing the attested anchor pair (his address word at oshb:Song.2.2, hers at oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) as the reason this row opens at Song.2.4; delete the 'no formula anchor survives past Song.2.3' phrasing as a driver. Re-cut the Song.2.6 citation as a curly-quoted, exact-case run paired with its inline web: ref. device_notes: name the swept object and unit for the ahavah claim (10 verses, 11 tokens). Tests the cure must pass: the span must still open at Song.2.4 (a re-cut to Song.2.3 fails the whole-held dialogue-zone rule and splits the oshb:Song.2.2/oshb:Song.2.3 anchor pair -- this is the test that kills the challenge's own proposed replacement); the WEB run must pass an exact-case contiguous substring check against that witness; the ahavah citation must name object and unit before its digit. Span change: none proposed.

orders.challenge_claim: No tier-1 marker stands at the row's opening cut; an undisclosed apple-token link straddles that same seam; the row's no-addressee ground is contradicted by the imperatives in its own middle verse and is inconsistent with the criterion applied at Song.2.15; and the closing seam is argued only from an English rendering while the embrace colon's recurrence before the later adjuration goes undisclosed.
orders.grounds: Three sub-findings upheld exactly on re-derivation, one re-labelled. (1) Same defect as the LF item at the cut: verified, no tier-1 in-verse marker at 2:3|2:4. (2) Cross-seam token link verified with the object named: the stem shared by the two apple forms sweeps to 4 verses at skeleton tier (MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5 -- the offset-zone dual is arithmetically right), two of them on opposite sides of this row's own opening seam, and both witnesses carry the link; the row discloses nothing. The tier is skeleton, not byte: the two attested forms differ in number and pointing, so the honest statement is a shared-stem link, not a formula recurrence. (3) The no-addressee ground is byte-false INSIDE the row's own span: סַמְּכ֨וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי (oshb:Song.2.5, tier: byte) is two plural imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes -- an explicit addressee -- and that other witness renders them as imperatives too; the inconsistency charge also holds, since the plural-imperative-addressee feature is what drives the cut at Song.2.15 in this same cluster. (4) RE-LABELLED inside the uphold: the byte fact is verified -- וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte) recurs at MT 8:3 at SKELETON tier only (skeleton sweep of that colon: 2 verses, MT 2:6 and MT 8:3; the byte and accent tiers each return 1 verse because the later site carries an extra meteg, and the verse's left-hand colon differs by a prefixed preposition and sweeps to 1 verse, which is how the pair escapes an exact sweep) -- and it stands immediately before the MT 8:4 adjuration, so an embrace-line-then-adjuration sequence recurs; but that parallel SUPPORTS this row's own 2:6|2:7 close rather than arguing a rival to it, so it is an undisclosed strengthener, not a rival cut. The closing-seam complaint stands on its own: the seam is argued from an English rendering with no Hebrew quoted at the closing verse.
orders.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the no-addressee ground outright and re-state the span's texture from its own bytes (a first-person voice that includes an addressed plural imperative at Song.2.5); ground the closing seam in Hebrew by quoting the embrace colon from oshb:Song.2.6 (tier: byte) rather than in translation. device_notes: disclose the apple-stem link across the opening seam with its tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 4 verses, MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5), and disclose the embrace-colon recurrence at MT 8:3 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) as a parallel supporting this close. Reconcile the plural-imperative criterion with its use as a cut driver at Song.2.15 in one clause. Tests the cure must pass: no stated ground may survive that the row's own span bytes contradict (the Song.2.5 imperatives are the test that killed the original); every cross-seam device named must carry tier AND digit AND its offset-zone dual where one applies; the same feature must not be a driver in one row and absent from the criterion in another. Span change: none proposed.

orders.challenge_claim: LF: the Song.2.14 WEB citation is verbatim in content but straight-quoted rather than curly, a register-only defect. OL: the frame-verb wording attributed to web:Song.2.10 is not that witness's rendering, and the blossom-token chain straddling the closing seam is undisclosed; the second-feminine-singular marker case and the disclosure symmetry are otherwise the cluster's strongest.
orders.grounds: DISTINCT defects. The refinement is of severity and of which finding is load-bearing: the LF item rates this row's only defect 'low' and register-only, which understates the row, because the substantive defect it missed is a misattributed witness rendering. Verified: the row gives the frame verb as an answered-and-said wording attributed to web:Song.2.10, but that witness reads “My beloved spoke, and said to me,” (web:Song.2.10) -- the row's string fails a substring check against that witness even case-insensitively, so the wording ascribed to the cited witness is not its wording. The Hebrew עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) does support an answered-gloss, but this row quotes no Hebrew at that clause, so its own frame-verb ground is translation-dependent on a rendering that witness does not carry. LF's register point is separately verified and real: the Song.2.14 run is an exact-case verbatim substring of that witness but is delimited with straight marks, and this cluster carries zero curly-quoted WEB runs while the corpus uses the curly convention elsewhere -- so the departure is local, not a book-wide convention. OL's cross-seam finding verified with object and tier: the blossom token is byte at each of its own sites, סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13, tier: byte) and סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte), and the link between them is skeleton tier, sweeping to 3 verses book-wide (MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12 -- dual arithmetically right), two of the three sitting on opposite sides of this row's closing cut. Verified as correct and NOT defective: the disclosure symmetry OL credits is real -- both ketiv/qere-bearing verses in span and both marked verses in span are named, and no quoted slice crosses the ketiv word inside the Song.2.13 line.
orders.remedy: boundary_rationale: either replace the frame-verb wording with that witness's actual rendering, curly-quoted with its inline web: ref, or re-anchor the ground on the Hebrew frame verb spliced from oshb:Song.2.10 (tier: byte) with the gloss marked as a gloss; re-cut the Song.2.14 citation into curly quotes with its inline web: ref. device_notes: disclose the blossom-token link across the closing seam with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12). orders.grounds: Byte-false as stated, confirmed by an independent word-bound sweep. The first 1cs form in the book's flow stands inside this row's own verse - הָפִ֥יחִי גַנִּ֖י (byte, oshb:Song.4.16), the woman's imperative to the wind - and the next in the man's speech at בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1). Both witnesses concur: “My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.” (web:Song.4.12) and “Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out.” (web:Song.4.16). The row's boundary_rationale therefore locates a form in Song.4.8-Song.4.15 that is not there, and carries that half of its voice-shift argument with no quoted form at all, which the engagement standard bars for a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; strongest_rejected_alternative repeats the same male-voice premise, so the defect is duplicated in a second field. The seam itself survives and no boundary change is proposed: יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) is the her-word-for-him anchor (dodi-exact: 24 verses; distinct from the 28-verse dod-family, from the defective 'your loves' form standing twice inside MT 4:10 in the man's mouth, and from the plural at oshb:Song.5.1), and the shift actually attested runs her 'my garden' to 'his garden' INSIDE this one verse - tier-1 in-verse formula anchor, which is stronger evidence than the cross-unit shift the row asserted. Severity holds at medium rather than high because the cure is a re-cut sentence over evidence already in the row's own verse.
orders.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P01-019): delete the parenthetical locating 'my garden' in Song.4.8-Song.4.15 and re-cut the shift to the one attested inside this verse - her spliced 1cs garden form against the 3ms garden form in the same verse, both tier-labeled byte at oshb:Song.4.16 - keeping the her-word-for-him anchor as the tier-1 driver and naming its object (dodi-exact, 24 verses) where any digit is carried. Mirror the identical correction into strongest_rejected_alternative, which repeats the male-voice premise. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): a word-bound gan-family sweep restricted to MT 4:8-4:15 must return the form the sentence claims - it currently returns no 1cs-suffixed form at any tier - and every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim must ship a spliced, tier-labeled form at the ref it is claimed for.

orders.grounds: DISTINCT defects, both upheld; the two primaries did not overlap on this row, and both agree the boundaries themselves are sound (re-derived: the formula opens the movement immediately after the adjuration bracket, and עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) is a genuine tier-1 frame verb introducing quoted speech). LF upheld: the row presents 'he stands behind our wall... he glances through the lattice' as one run against a single web: ref; that witness reads “Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.” (web:Song.2.9), so a whole sentence is dropped inside the ellipsis and the second fragment lower-cases a verse-initial word -- the presented run fails an exact-case check and fails a contiguous check even case-insensitively; delimiters are straight, not curly. OL upheld: the row's recurrence claim carries no tier at all, and the tier is not byte -- ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֔י (oshb:Song.2.8, tier: byte) reaches only accent_stripped at the second site, whose attested shape is ק֣וֹל דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק (oshb:Song.5.2, tier: byte); the honest object is a 2-verse recurrence at accent_stripped/skeleton tier (MT 2:8, MT 5:2), so the DIGIT the row cites is right and only the tier is missing. OL's bracket upheld with its object verified: the gazelle-and-fawn colon לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.9, tier: byte) and לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) share a 19-character consonantal run whose skeleton sweep returns 3 verses (MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14); the two chapter-2 members sit on opposite sides of this row's closing seam and bracket MT 2:8-2:17, and no row in the stretch discloses it. The spelling-split caution is verified too: the likeness verb is written with vav at MT 2:9 (skeleton sweep: 1 verse) and without it at MT 2:17 and MT 8:14 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses), so an exact sweep of either spelling hides a member.
orders.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the Song.2.9 citation as a contiguous curly-quoted exact-case run, or as two separately-quoted runs each paired with its own inline web: ref -- no ellipsis across a dropped sentence. Tier-label the qol-dodi recurrence at the tier a collation proves (byte at oshb:Song.2.8; accent_stripped at the second site, attested there in a longer shape), keeping the 2-verse digit. device_notes: disclose the gazelle-and-fawn colon across the closing seam with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14) and name the likeness-verb spelling split before any digit is reused. Tests the cure must pass: the WEB run must pass a contiguous exact-case substring check against that witness (the dropped sentence is the test that killed the original); the recurrence claim must carry the tier a collation returns at EVERY cited site, not at the first only; the cross-seam device must be disclosed with tier and digit.
